newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish ROP party against banking, oil sector sales.
newsitem.headline: Polish ROP party against banking, oil sector sales.

text.p: The opposition Movement for the Reconstruction of Poland (ROP), unveiling its programme for this year's parliamentary polls, said on Tuesday it was opposed to any privatisation of banks, oil and the defence industry.

The party also advocated an active state role in reforming the economy to bring it closer to Western development levels, PAP news agency quoted ROP economic expert Dariusz Grabowski as telling a news conference in the southern city of Krakow.

The ruling coalition of ex-communists and a peasant party plans to sell banks, oil refining and distribution companies through transactions with strategic investors and public offerings. It has yet to decide what to do with the defence sector.
Recent opinion polls showed that the ROP -- a non-parliamentary group, advocating pro-family, patriotic, anti-communist and often populist values -- enjoys support of between six and 10 percent.

Analysts say that, after elections due around September this year, ROP could form a government with the Solidarity Electoral Action (AWS), now the strongest group in opposition to the four-year-old ruling coalition of ex-communist Democratic Left Alliance (SLD) and the Peasant Party (PSL).

PAP quoted Grabowski as saying that his party backed a tax system that would favour families and that it wanted to use proceeds from privatisation in the planned reform of the ailing pension system. Most other Polish parties, including those of the ruling coalition, also want to finance the much-needed reform with sales of state-owned companies.
The ROP also promised to stimulate growth of small and medium-size firms and to offer investment relief for big companies, PAP said.
The party -- led by Jan Olszewski, who served as prime minister in the first half of 1992 -- would also subsidise housing construction, PAP reported. -- Marcin Grajewski +48 22 653 9700
